gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Heavy and wide-tracked, Dogica keeps its lowercase close to capital height while Noto Sans Hebrew follows beneath. Dogica commands; Noto Sans Hebrew fills its line with a dominant midsection.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-kr: Dogica spreads its wide tracking across every heavy, commanding line. Noto Sans KR reads smoothly over many lines, its generous curve gaps and big x-height keeping the text open.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Dogica is heavy and widely tracked, each curve left clearly open. It commands best; Noto Sans Mahajani does its best work with a tall lowercase and a funnel-shaped e.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-saurashtr: Dogica is heavy and commanding, with wide tracking and a clear opening at the end of every curve. But Noto Sans Saurashtra does its best work quietly, with counters that stay connected to the outside.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog keeps its middle zone dominant, curves generously open. Weight is the real story: Dogica lands heavy and wide-tracked while the Tagalog face stays clean and open.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-prompt: Wide tracking is the signature of Dogica, giving heavy letters room while lowercase climbs nearly to capital height. Prompt then keeps things approachable with oversized small letters and open apertures.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-arimo: Playful but commanding, Early GameBoy stretches its tracking wide and lets the x-height climb. Arimo supplies the sans-serif text, its mean line tall and the gaps in round letters generous.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-athiti: Athiti keeps a high mean line and see-through s shapes. What stands out most is the weight: Early GameBoy varies its strokes like thread against yarn, while Athiti keeps horizontals no thinner than verticals.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-biryani: Glassy, widely spaced and quietly tapered, Early GameBoy has a commanding streak with a playful edge. Yet Biryani does its best work as monoline sans-serif text, with a large eye on every e.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-carrois-goth: Wide-set and playful, Early GameBoy lifts its x-height high and lets stroke widths shift just enough to notice. And Carrois Gothic moves down the page smoothly, its open c and high x-height keeping the text modern.
